questions.question: How many bits are in an IPv4 address?
questions.explanation: IPv4 addresses consist of four 8-bit octets.

option_explanations.A: 128 bits is the size of an IPv6 address.
option_explanations.B: 16 bits account for only two IPv4 octets.
option_explanations.C: 48 bits is the size of a standard Ethernet MAC address.
option_explanations.D: IPv4 addresses consist of four 8-bit octets.

questions.question: Which decimal value cannot appear as an IPv4 address octet?

option_explanations.A: 0 fits in eight bits, even though whole-address rules may restrict particular uses.

questions.question: A packet leaves a host with IPv4 TTL 64 and passes three forwarding routers. Each subtracts one. What TTL arrives at the destination?
questions.explanation: The packet's TTL decreases by one per forwarding router in this scenario. 64 minus three gives 61.

option_explanations.C: 62 would imply only two forwarding decrements.
option_explanations.D: The packet's TTL decreases by one per forwarding router in this scenario. 64 minus three gives 61.

questions.question: Which IPv4 header field indicates that the payload is ICMP?
questions.explanation: The Protocol field identifies the encapsulated protocol. ICMP is protocol number 1.

option_explanations.A: Total Length gives the IPv4 datagram size.
option_explanations.B: Identification helps associate fragments of a datagram.
option_explanations.C: The Protocol field identifies the encapsulated protocol. ICMP is protocol number 1.
option_explanations.D: Time to Live limits how far the packet can be forwarded.

questions.question: A capture shows IPv4 Total Length 84 and IHL 5. How many bytes follow the IPv4 header inside the datagram?
questions.explanation: IHL counts 32-bit words, so five words form a 20-byte header. Subtract the header from the total length to get 64 bytes.

option_explanations.A: 104 adds the 20-byte header to a total that already includes it.
option_explanations.B: IHL counts 32-bit words, so five words form a 20-byte header. Subtract the header from the total length to get 64 bytes.
option_explanations.C: 79 treats IHL 5 as five bytes instead of five 32-bit words.
option_explanations.D: 84 includes the IPv4 header as well as its payload.

questions.question: A host formerly obtained its address, prefix and router through DHCP. After conversion to static settings it reaches local peers, but it has no route to remote networks. Which missing setting explains the behavior?
questions.explanation: A usable static address and mask allow on-link communication. A default gateway supplies a next hop for other destinations.

option_explanations.A: A usable static address and mask allow on-link communication. A default gateway supplies a next hop for other destinations.
option_explanations.B: Static addressing does not need a DHCP lease duration.
option_explanations.C: A DNS suffix affects name lookup rather than routing to a known IP.
option_explanations.D: The local Ethernet interface is already reaching peers, and its MAC cannot supply a default route.

questions.question: Besides an address, which useful pair can an IPv4 DHCP server supply to a client?

options.B: Switch port duplex and fiber connector
options.C: TCP acknowledgment number and receive window

questions.explanation: DHCP options can supply the client mask and default-router information.

option_explanations.A: A MAC and FCS belong to Ethernet, and the FCS is calculated for each frame.
option_explanations.B: Those are physical link properties rather than DHCP address options.
option_explanations.D: DHCP options can supply the client mask and default-router information.

questions.question: Why is the IPv4 header checksum updated by a forwarding router even when the payload stays the same?

options.A: The destination IP is replaced with the gateway IP
options.B: Forwarding changes a header field such as TTL
options.C: The TCP ports always change at each hop
options.D: The checksum covers the Ethernet source address

questions.explanation: The checksum protects the IPv4 header, so a TTL change requires an update.

option_explanations.A: Ordinary forwarding changes next-hop link-layer addresses, not the IPv4 destination.
option_explanations.B: The checksum protects the IPv4 header, so a TTL change requires an update.
option_explanations.C: TCP ports are normally unchanged in ordinary forwarding.
option_explanations.D: The IPv4 header checksum does not cover Ethernet fields.

questions.question: A router receives an IPv4 packet with TTL 1 that would otherwise be forwarded. What normally occurs?

options.A: The packet is forwarded unchanged as a broadcast
options.B: The packet is discarded and the router may send ICMP Time Exceeded
options.C: The router sends a TCP reset to the destination
options.D: The router forwards it with TTL 255

questions.explanation: Forwarding would exhaust TTL, so the packet is dropped. ICMP Time Exceeded can report this condition.

option_explanations.A: Decrementing TTL makes it zero, which prevents forwarding.
option_explanations.B: Forwarding would exhaust TTL, so the packet is dropped. ICMP Time Exceeded can report this condition.
option_explanations.C: An intermediate router normally reports expiration with ICMP rather than TCP RST.
option_explanations.D: TTL is not reset to 255 in ordinary forwarding.

questions.question: A workstation was switched from static settings to DHCP and no lease was obtained. Which first check directly tests whether the intended address source exists on that network?

options.A: Check whether the address in the old manual entry is in DNS
options.B: Verify that a DHCP service or relay is available for the LAN
options.C: Compare the manual gateway with the switch's MAC aging timer
options.D: Inspect the peer's TCP receive window

questions.explanation: A DHCP client needs a reachable DHCP service, directly or through a relay.

option_explanations.A: DNS records do not establish whether a DHCP server can answer discovery.
option_explanations.B: A DHCP client needs a reachable DHCP service, directly or through a relay.
option_explanations.C: A switch's MAC aging timer is unrelated to whether a DHCP service can be reached.
option_explanations.D: IPv4 DHCP uses UDP, not a TCP peer window.
